reviews.title: The cliched story. The promise and then the pivot from 5 to 1
reviews.text:
Like so many other apps and new businesses, the timeline here ends up feeling the same. At first, the experience is free or competitively affordable relative to its features. You start to use it and believe in it. Support is from actual humans and the tech continues to grow and stay seamless. Then the “pro” and “elite premium” tiers get introduced. But now you’ve been using it to store all your passwords. So what’s another $100 a year for the sanity of password protection and retention continuity across devices. 

But then things change again, the “new” features are promised but never work. Maintenance of status quo from years before now gets regurgitated as new horizon possibilities of only we pay a little more. But those services like safari extensions or seamless integration with iOS apps never happen. And more and more glitches start to happen without immediate update pushes/fixes. We’re a captive user at this point. So now the support starts to become harder and harder to access. In fact. At some point you will be asked to upload screen shots of proof of premium purchase and invoice history to have access to support. Even after you do. You will get a bad general faq response email from a fake human support person that feels almost too insultingly generic to be anything like the definition of gaslighting. You will follow up with more information. You will receive the next form letter that feels slightly more believable as having actually read your issue but still basicall

reviews.title: Worse than terrible
reviews.text:
Some apps you can just shrug off and not use if they aren’t working for you. But as a password “manager” this gets embedded within all your devices and if it doesn’t behave properly you are truly cooked, and you have invested heavily in it. I forever have timing issues with this, where it conflicts with the apple keychain so when  I uodate a password, both apple and LastPass through up dialogs, but you have to answer apple first, and frequently I “lose” the LastPass so the password is not updated.  Sync across devices is profoundly unreliable as I learned from my recent purchase of a new iPad. The first thing I configured was LastPass in the vain hope that it would copy all the info from the old iPad (I had already done an apple from old iPad to new iPad but I though I could also rely on the LastPass vault to maintain passwords across all devices) 
I have had MANY instances of LastPass serving up an OLD/obsolete password and since I try to use high security passwords I am forced into a “forgot password” dialog (ironically) to reset, but LastPass often doesn’t pickup the new password, in the case at hand prompting this it even suggested I use the one-off verification code as the username!! 
At the end of the day it is wholly unreliable, leaves me with no confidence and has been the source of continuous frustration.  I am ripping it out of all my devices.

It was bullet proof but now I have the extension logged in but it won’t save changes or new passwords. It goes through the process with all the prompts but then throughs an error message about not being able to complete the task at that time try again later. Then I tried to turn on the Face ID to logon to my iPhone LP app and I set it to Face ID it seems to take the setting change / turned it on and then it works one time or for one day but then it turns off that option / functionality so it is highly frustrating. All support tells me to do it refresh through options or uninstall the app. So I would uninstall everyday? ?  It was never this buggy 6-12 months ago. I was a big supporter and told many many people and orgs to use last pass but I will have a real problem promoting last pass any longer until there are some big changes over the next few months. I have a Keeper account and that seems to be not as buggy so I may need to switch.
